verses.gurmukhi: ਬਿਰਖੈੈ ਬਇਆਰ ਲਾਗੈ ਜੈਸੇ ਹਰ ਰਾਤਿ ਪਾਤਿ ਪੰਛੀ ਨ ਧੀਰਜ ਕਰਿ ਠਉਰ ਠਹਿਰਾਤ ਹੈ ॥
verses.translit_en: birakhaiai biaar laagai jaise har raat paat pa(n)chhee na dheeraj kar Thaur Thahiraat hai ||

en.bdb: Just as the leaves and branches of a tree start trembling under the influence of fast wind and even the birds lose trust of their nests;

verses.gurmukhi: ਸਰਵਰ ਘਾਮ ਲਾਗੈ ਬਾਰਜ ਬਿਲਖ ਮੁਖ ਪ੍ਰਾਨ ਅੰਤ ਹੰਤ ਜਲ ਜੰਤ ਅਕੁਲਾਤ ਹੈ ॥
verses.translit_en: saravar ghaam laagai baaraj bilakh mukh praan a(n)t ha(n)t jal ja(n)t akulaat hai ||

en.bdb: Just as lotus flowers whither away under the sharp heat of the Sun and aquatic life of the water feels distressed as if their lives were coming to an end;

verses.gurmukhi: ਸਾਰਦੂਲ ਦੇਖੈ ਮ੍ਰਿਗਮਾਲ ਦਲ ਚਿਤ ਬਨ ਵਾਸ ਮੈ ਨ ਤ੍ਰਾਸ ਕਰਿ ਆਸ੍ਰਮ ਸੁਹਾਤ ਹੈ ॥
verses.translit_en: saaradhool dhekhai miragamaal dhal chit ban vaas mai na traas kar aasram suhaat hai ||

en.bdb: Just as the herd of deers find solace and safety in their small hiding places in the jungle when they see the lion in the vicinity;

verses.gurmukhi: ਤੈਸੇ ਗੁਰ ਆਂਗ ਸ੍ਵਾਂਗਿ ਭਏ ਭੈ ਚਕਤਿ ਸਿਖ ਦੁਖਤਿ ਉਦਾਸ ਬਾਸ ਅਤਿ ਬਿਲਲਾਤ ਹੈ ॥੪੦੨॥
verses.translit_en: taise gur aa(n)g savaiaa(n)g bhe bhai chakat sikh dhukhat udhaas baas at bilalaat hai ||402||

en.bdb: Similarly, the Sikhs of the Guru are frightened, amazed, distressed and morose seeing the body/limbs of a spurious Guru marked with artificial marks of recognition. Even the Sikhs most close to the Guru feel restless.  (402)
